bug_semantics: An authenticated student could supply a course ID to teacher/admin course routes. The clearest data-bearing path was POST /api/analytics/course: it accepted courseId from the request, used a Supabase service-role client, and returned the course roster, names, email addresses, lesson/exercise totals, per-student completion, grades, submissions, and last-login data without checking that the requester was an admin or tutor. The UI merely hid the analytics/people/submissions navigation from students, so a crafted /courses/<course-id>/analytics URL still caused the privileged request; the same UI-only authorization pattern exposed the other advisory-listed course pages.
flaw_origin: PR #574's first member commit created both the hidden-from-students analytics navigation item and the service-role analytics endpoint, but added no server-side role check. The public mainline commit ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817 is a squash aggregate; decomposition identifies 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 as the smallest commit that first wrote the vulnerable endpoint and route.
ai_marker: BIC commit object 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 has author and committer 'emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com>' and message 'feat: added anaytics for the course page'; `git cat-file -p` shows no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI tool trailer, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-mh75-3225-9wcj / CVE-2025-65670 names ClassroomIO 0.1.13 and reproduces with a student changing the course ID in /courses/<id>/analytics, attendance, submissions, people, and marks URLs; it reports disclosure before the client returns to its restricted state.

`git show v0.1.13:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts` shows POST reading `{ courseId }` from the body and immediately calling `getCourseAnalytics(courseId)`; that function selects all group members and profiles, lessons, exercises, submissions, grades, progress, and last-login values, with no requester identity or role comparison. `git show v0.1.13:apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/functions/supabase.server.ts` shows the client uses PRIVATE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE, bypassing row-level policy protection.

`git show v0.1.13:apps/dashboard/src/lib/components/Course/components/Navigation/index.svelte` shows the analytics, people, submissions, landing-page, and settings links are hidden with `return !isStudent`, while `git show v0.1.13:apps/dashboard/src/routes/courses/[id]/analytics/+page.svelte` shows the route itself has no RoleBasedSecurity wrapper and POSTs the URL-derived course ID to the privileged analytics endpoint.

GitHub's first-party `GET /repos/classroomio/classroomio/pulls/574/commits` lists seven PR members in order: 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3, 496e98fa2babb38df4d3fcea3c3f5fb4c30c770d, 93ed4e6f8dc83f29dd9e57312df8314647fb1e8a, 3a87cfd627c136a4b66f8ff35a65831495d85a51, 644101f69b9ba975ca15a11170ae3b32bdd5ae6b, 1ae1616ffd92804a99ffec34a10e77809270fb2c, and b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505. The final member tree equals squash landing ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817's tree, proving the decomposition.

`git show 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3 -- apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts apps/dashboard/src/routes/courses/[id]/analytics/+page.svelte apps/dashboard/src/lib/components/Course/components/Navigation/index.svelte` shows the BIC newly adds all three: the role-hidden link, unguarded page, and 276-line service-role endpoint. `git log -S 'const { courseId } = await request.json();' b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505 -- <endpoint>` and `git log -L 11,16:<endpoint> b9fe4d54712aeab8468b94ed6fd8c7ce7a777505` both resolve the vulnerable request handling to 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3.

Direct parent verification: `git cat-file -e '7d150ea5004f466e35d839b6344580866f855abe:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/analytics/course/+server.ts'` fails with 'path ... does not exist'; the BIC diff is a new file from /dev/null. The analytics page is likewise new in the BIC.

Version boundary: `git tag --contains ec3875bac2c68868f77bd456e070b0f3cc194817 --sort=version:refname` places the vulnerable landing in releases beginning v0.1.2, including advisory-named v0.1.13 and every 0.2.x tag through 0.2.11. `git show 0.2.11:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/courses/analytics/+server.ts` still permits a course member and treats the object returned by checkUserCoursePermissions as a boolean, so it does not enforce admin/tutor role. `git tag --contains 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052` starts at v0.3.0, making v0.3.0 the first tagged fixed release.

`git show b4326e6517e0b9f058dfe86c173b0c10d58c3b35` is the minimal direct fix: on GET /:courseId/analytics it replaces courseMemberMiddleware (which permits students) with courseTeamMemberMiddleware (admin/tutor members and org admins). The member was squash-landed in main as 1e9a82e912736d87092715fae13329b76254d052; `git show v0.3.0:apps/api/src/routes/course/course.ts` shows authMiddleware plus courseTeamMemberMiddleware on the analytics handler.

`git cat-file -p 4198d15f360e8f1327f262e5d0bba03d895cc9c3` supplies the BIC-only AI check: human author/committer emmanuel, ordinary feature message, and no trailers. The later direct fix is authored by Cursor Agent, but protocol excludes AI-only-on-fix evidence from the BIC verdict.
reasoning: The security boundary must be enforced where privileged data is read, not by hiding client navigation. The first PR #574 member created a service-role endpoint keyed solely by attacker-controlled courseId and simultaneously hid its link from students, making the missing server-side admin/tutor check the root cause rather than a later move or refactor. Its immediate parent has neither the endpoint nor page, and both -S and -L trace the vulnerable request line to that member. The squash landing was therefore decomposed rather than selected as the BIC. The eventual direct patch explicitly states that courseMemberMiddleware allowed students and changes analytics to courseTeamMemberMiddleware; its squash landing is present in the first fixed tag v0.3.0. Because the BIC commit object has no AI marker and human identities only, the required BIC-only judgment is NOT_AI even though an AI agent authored the later fix.
